# Consumer-specific names that must never appear in generic Continuum code.
#
# The rule this file enforces: a value that is true of one consumer and false of
# another does not live in Continuum. It resolves from `.github/continuum.yml`,
# from repository `vars`, from repository secrets, or from the consumer's own
# scripts and manifests. Continuum carries the mechanism, never the fact.
#
# The single deliberate exception is the exact Continuum release reference in a
# reusable-workflow `uses:` (and in a SHA-pinned `uses:` of a Continuum action),
# because GitHub requires that spelling to be literal. Every other literal is a
# hard-code waiting to be edited in a release.
#
# This list is data, not code. The scanner greps the generic surface for exactly
# these expressions and the contract-core guard greps for the same file, so a
# new consumer name is banned by adding one line here and nowhere else.
#
# One extended regular expression per line; blank lines and `#` lines are
# ignored; a match on any scanned line fails the build.

# --- Consumer identity ------------------------------------------------------
# Owner login, product name, sibling repositories, and the branch/marker
# vocabulary inherited from an earlier consumer control plane.
kodmial
nanodictate
kodmai
runtime[-_]lab
runtime[-_]worker

# --- Provider facts ---------------------------------------------------------
# A model identifier is a repository operational value, not a Continuum default.
# The shape is banned rather than the current identifier, because a new model
# name is the most likely way this value creeps back in, and a ban on today's
# spelling would only notice after somebody had already picked tomorrow's.
(?<![.\w])opencode/(?!issue)[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*

# --- Release escape refs ----------------------------------------------------
# An input that chooses which Continuum the reusable workflow then checks out is
# a way to run something other than the release the caller pinned in `uses:`.
engine_ref
